name: Savannah, Georgia
kicker: Georgia’s oldest city, founded 1733 · End of Sherman’s March to the Sea
briefing: In 1733, James Oglethorpe and a shipload of English colonists climbed a bluff above a river near the Atlantic and laid out Savannah, the first city in Georgia, around a grid of shady public squares that still exist today. Eli Whitney built his cotton gin at a plantation nearby, and in 1864 General William T. Sherman ended his March to the Sea here, offering the city to Abraham Lincoln as a “Christmas gift.” Juliette Gordon Low founded the Girl Scouts here in 1912.

qb.tip: Search QBReader for this answer line (Middle School + Easy High School, power-marked) to see how real tossups clue it.

tossups.p: With help from the interpreter Mary Musgrove, this city’s founder made friends with Tomochichi [“TOH-moh-CHEE-chee”], the leader of the Yamacraw [“YAM-uh-kraw”] people, who allowed English colonists to settle on a bluff above a river. Tomochichi later sailed to London and met King George II.
tossups.r: That founder was James Oglethorpe. For 10 points, name this city founded in 1733, the first city in the colony of Georgia.

tossups.p: The bench scenes in the film _Forrest Gump_ were shot in this city’s Chippewa Square, one of 22 surviving public squares out of the 24 laid out as the city grew. Those squares follow the founder’s plan, in which each neighborhood, or ward, was built around a central square.
tossups.r: That plan was drawn up by James Oglethorpe. For 10 points, name this city on the Georgia coast, the colony’s first settlement.

tossups.p: In October 1779, the Polish cavalry officer Casimir Pulaski [“puh-LASS-kee”] was mortally wounded in a failed French and American attack on this British-held city. Volunteers from the French colony of Saint-Domingue [“san doh-MANG”], now Haiti, also fought in that siege.
tossups.r: The British held this city for most of the rest of the war. For 10 points, name this Georgia port founded by James Oglethorpe in 1733.

tossups.p: At Mulberry Grove, a plantation upriver from this city owned by Catharine Greene, the widow of General Nathanael Greene, a young Yale graduate built a machine in 1793 that pulled the seeds out of cotton. The plantation’s manager, Phineas Miller, became that inventor’s business partner.
tossups.r: That inventor was Eli Whitney. For 10 points, name this Georgia port city founded by James Oglethorpe.

tossups.p: In December 1864, Union soldiers stormed Fort McAllister, opening a supply line to the sea south of this city. Days later, Confederate general William Hardee pulled his troops out across the river into South Carolina, and Union troops marched in.
tossups.r: Their commander then offered this city to Abraham Lincoln as a “Christmas gift.” For 10 points, name this Georgia city where William T. Sherman ended his March to the Sea.

tossups.p: In January 1865, Secretary of War Edwin Stanton and a Union general met with a group of Black church leaders in this city, led by the Baptist minister Garrison Frazier. Days later, that general issued Special Field Orders No. 15 here, setting aside coastal land for freed families.
tossups.r: That general, William T. Sherman, had just ended his March to the Sea here. For 10 points, name this Georgia port.

tossups.p: In 1819, a ship named for this city left its port on May 22 and became the first steamship to cross the Atlantic Ocean, though it used its sails for most of the trip. That departure date is now celebrated as National Maritime Day.
tossups.r: For 10 points, name this Georgia port city, where Juliette Gordon Low founded the Girl Scouts in 1912.

tossups.p: In April 1862, Union rifled cannons fired from Tybee Island broke through the thick brick walls of Fort Pulaski, which guarded the river approach to this city. That success showed that old masonry forts could no longer stand up to modern artillery.
tossups.r: For 10 points, name this Georgia port, which William T. Sherman captured at the end of his March to the Sea.

tossups.p: In March 1861, Confederate Vice President Alexander Stephens gave his “Cornerstone Speech” in this city, saying that the new Confederacy rested on slavery. Before the Civil War, this city’s port shipped huge amounts of cotton grown across Georgia.
tossups.r: For 10 points, name this city that William T. Sherman offered to Abraham Lincoln as a “Christmas gift” in 1864.

tossups.p: John Wesley, the founder of Methodism, served as a minister in this city in the 1730s, and George Whitefield [“WIT-feeld”] founded the Bethesda orphanage nearby in 1740. Jewish settlers arrived in this city only months after it was founded.
tossups.r: For 10 points, name this city founded by James Oglethorpe, the first in the colony of Georgia.

tossups.p: The songwriter Johnny Mercer, who wrote the words to “Moon River,” and the author Flannery O’Connor were both born in this city. John Berendt’s 1994 nonfiction bestseller _Midnight in the Garden of Good and Evil_ is set here.
tossups.r: Juliette Gordon Low founded the Girl Scouts here in 1912. For 10 points, name this Georgia city founded by James Oglethorpe.

tossups.p: In 1912, a woman inspired by Robert Baden-Powell gathered 18 girls in this city to form the first troop of a group first called the American Girl Guides, which took a new name the next year.
tossups.r: That woman, Juliette Gordon Low, founded the Girl Scouts. For 10 points, name this Georgia city, where James Oglethorpe’s colonists landed in 1733.

tossups.p: Every March, the fountain in this city’s Forsyth Park is dyed green before one of the largest St. Patrick’s Day parades in the United States. An art and design college founded here in 1978, known as SCAD, has restored many of this city’s historic buildings.
tossups.r: For 10 points, name this Georgia port city, where Sherman’s March to the Sea ended in 1864.

tossups.p: A ship named for this city, launched in 1959, became the world’s first nuclear-powered cargo and passenger ship. This city’s port, on the river that forms much of the border between Georgia and South Carolina, is one of the busiest container ports in the United States.
tossups.r: James Oglethorpe founded it in 1733. For 10 points, name this city, the oldest in Georgia.

tossups.p: The colony that began in this city was meant partly as a buffer between South Carolina and Spanish Florida, and its Trustees at first banned slavery there. This city’s founder had led a campaign in Parliament to improve conditions in debtors’ prisons.
tossups.r: That founder, James Oglethorpe, landed here in 1733. For 10 points, name this first city of the colony of Georgia.

A steamship named for it made the first Atlantic crossing partly by steam (1819); National Maritime Day (May 22) marks its departure

trap.title: Start or end of the march?
trap.body: Sherman’s March to the Sea started in Atlanta, which his army captured in September 1864, and ended in Savannah in December 1864, so mixing up the two cities loses the tossup. “Georgia” alone is not enough when the question asks for a city. The Savannah River, Fort Pulaski, and Savannah, Tennessee (where Ulysses S. Grant had his headquarters during the Battle of Shiloh), are different answers.
trap.fix: John Bell Hood, “Atlanta is ours,” and Sherman’s letter to Mayor Calhoun mean Atlanta; Fort McAllister, Hardee’s retreat, and the “Christmas gift” mean Savannah. Oglethorpe, Tomochichi, the squares, and the Girl Scouts also mean Savannah.
trap.line: Real answer line: Savannah, Georgia (do not accept “Georgia” alone)
